channel.title: Signal & Shield
channel.description: A daily briefing on cybersecurity and AI, by Simon Boadi

item.title: An exploited Azure API Management flaw exposes customer secrets, Bell Canada blames an agentic hacker, and Anthropic lets Claude approve pull requests
item.description: Microsoft confirmed that a flaw in Azure API Management Classic tiers was used to go after stored credentials, which Norwegian authorities tied to attacks on energy firms. Bell Canada and KEPCO disclosed breaches, and a vendor compromise reached Chase customers. In AI, Anthropic and OpenAI shipped agent tools aimed at code review and live patching, Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang, and two states sued SpaceX over Grok.

item.title: ScreenConnect attacks hit MSPs, GL.iNet's cloud is used to plant router malware, and OpenAI proposes a speed limit for AI
item.description: Attackers are going after the tools that manage other systems: ScreenConnect deployments at managed service providers, GL.iNet's cloud management service, and a Microsoft Entra monitoring API. In AI, OpenRouter cut three providers after the prompt-theft research, OpenAI's chief scientist proposed industry-wide limits on model capability, and US officials warned that outages caused by patching AI-found flaws will continue.

item.title: A vCenter zero-day, AI agents that hack on their own, and a brutal week for AI stocks
item.description: A China-linked group exploited a critical VMware vCenter flaw for more than two months before it was patched, and Amazon documented autonomous AI agents finding and weaponizing a zero-day with no human steering. On the AI side, a canary experiment showed how leaky the inference supply chain is, Signal moved to block OS-level AI agents, and the Nasdaq had its worst week since 2020.
